title: Urinary trypsin inhibitor exerts multifaceted regulation of angiopoietin 2 in septic cardiomyopathy.
authors: Lu, Yi-Ni; Wang, Xiao-Han; Xu, Bo-Cheng; Zheng, Yu-Fen; Zhang, Xiong; Liu, Yi; Wang, Tian-Yin; Yu, Feng
one_liner_zh: 该文研究尿胰蛋白酶抑制剂在脓毒症心肌病中对血管生成素2的调控机制，涉及蛋白-蛋白结合预测与SPR验证，但核心为炎症信号通路与内皮功能，非蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合体系，且无AI/物理模拟方法。
abstract: Septic cardiomyopathy (SCM) represents one of the life-threatening manifestations of sepsis, for which specific therapies are currently lacking. The mechanism of action of urinary trypsin inhibitor (UTI), widely employed in treating acute inflammatory disorders, on SCM has remained elusive. Here, we observed that UTI alleviated cardiac function, reduced myocardial injury, and improved cardiac permeability in a cecum ligation and puncture (CLP)-induced sepsis mouse model. In addition, UTI significantly decreased serum and myocardial angiopoietin 2 (ANG2) levels in CLP mice, which is a biomarker associated with sepsis prognosis. In vitro experiments utilizing mouse myocardial microvascular endothelial cells (MMVECs) were conducted to explore the molecular mechanisms underlying UTI-mediated regulation of ANG2 expression, secretion, and its impacts on endothelial permeability and neutrophil adhesion. UTI mitigated endothelial barrier dysfunction and reduced neutrophil adherence following thrombin stimulation and ANG2 overexpression. The experiments further demonstrated that UTI-induced inhibition of ANG2 expression was related to the blockade of forkhead box O1 (FOXO1) and phosphorylated signal transducer and activator of transcription 3 (p-STAT3) nuclear transcription and that UTI disrupted ANG2 exocytosis by reducing intracellular Ca(2+) concentration, a mechanism distinct from other serine protease inhibitors. In addition, UTI ameliorated barrier impairment and neutrophil adhesion in ANG2 overexpression cells by restoring tyrosine kinase receptor 2 (Tie2)/protein kinase B (AKT) pathway phosphorylation. Docking predictions and surface plasmon resonance (SPR) further corroborated that UTI is strongly bound to ANG2. Altogether, our findings revealed a novel perspective wherein UTI functions as a multifaceted ANG2 inhibitor in SCM. Thus, ANG2 constitutes a promising therapeutic target for septic cardiomyopathy.
abstract_zh: 脓毒症心肌病（septic cardiomyopathy, SCM）是脓毒症的一种危及生命的表现形式，目前缺乏特异性治疗手段。尿胰蛋白酶抑制剂（urinary trypsin inhibitor, UTI）广泛用于治疗急性炎症性疾病，但其对SCM的作用机制尚不明确。在本研究中，我们观察到UTI在盲肠结扎穿刺（cecum ligation and puncture, CLP）诱导的脓毒症小鼠模型中改善了心脏功能、减轻了心肌损伤，并提高了心脏通透性。此外，UTI显著降低了CLP小鼠血清和心肌中血管生成素2（angiopoietin 2, ANG2）的水平，该因子是与脓毒症预后相关的生物标志物。我们利用小鼠心肌微血管内皮细胞（mouse myocardial microvascular endothelial cells, MMVECs）进行体外实验，以探讨UTI介导ANG2表达和分泌调控的分子机制，及其对内皮通透性和中性粒细胞黏附的影响。UTI缓解了凝血酶刺激和ANG2过表达后的内皮屏障功能障碍，并减少了中性粒细胞黏附。实验进一步表明，UTI诱导的ANG2表达抑制与叉头框蛋白O1（forkhead box O1, FOXO1）和磷酸化信号转导及转录激活因子3（phosphorylated signal transducer and activator of transcription 3, p-STAT3）核转录的阻断相关，且UTI通过降低细胞内Ca(2+)浓度来干扰ANG2的胞吐作用，这一机制不同于其他丝氨酸蛋白酶抑制剂。此外，UTI通过恢复酪氨酸激酶受体2（tyrosine kinase receptor 2, Tie2）/蛋白激酶B（protein kinase B, AKT）通路磷酸化，改善了ANG2过表达细胞中的屏障损伤和中性粒细胞黏附。对接预测和表面等离子体共振（surface plasmon resonance, SPR）进一步证实UTI与ANG2具有强结合能力。总之，我们的发现揭示了一个新视角，即UTI在SCM中作为多方面的ANG2抑制剂发挥作用。因此，ANG2构成了脓毒症心肌病的一个有前景的治疗靶点。
